accepted.s: Which constitutional amendment substituted the expression “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” as a ground for National Emergency under Article 352?
accepted.x: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978 replaced “internal disturbance” with “armed rebellion” in Article 352.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely numbered Constitutional Amendments and their specific changes.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A National Emergency under Article 352 may be proclaimed when there is an imminent danger of war, external aggression or armed rebellion. Such a proclamation may extend to:
o: The whole or any part of India
Any State only, but not the Union Territories
The whole of India and neighbouring countries
accepted.x: Article 352 permits a National Emergency to be proclaimed for the whole of India or for any part of India when the prescribed imminent danger exists.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of a constitutional power by separating “whole” from “whole or part.”
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the written advice required for proclamation of National Emergency:
1. The advice must be given by the Union Cabinet.
2. The requirement was inserted by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act.
3. The requirement is contained in Article 352(3).
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Article 352(3), inserted through the 44th Amendment, makes written advice of the Union Cabinet mandatory.
accepted.tq: Use the constitutional sub-clause and amendment together to verify all statements.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The approval of both Houses of Parliament for a proclamation of National Emergency must be obtained within:
accepted.x: Both Houses must approve a National Emergency proclamation within one month of its issue.
accepted.tq: Separate the one-month approval period for Article 352 from the two-month period under Article 360.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Once approved by Parliament, a proclamation of National Emergency continues for six months and may be extended further:
o: Only once, for another six months
Indefinitely, with parliamentary approval every six months
Until the next general election only
For a maximum of two years
accepted.x: After approval, the proclamation operates for six months and may continue indefinitely if Parliament approves its continuation every six months.
accepted.tq: Watch the contrast between a recurring six-month approval and a fixed maximum period.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the revocation of a National Emergency?
o: It can be revoked only by Parliament through a special majority.
The Supreme Court alone can revoke it after judicial review.
It automatically ends after six months even without parliamentary action.
The President may revoke it at any time, and must revoke it if the Lok Sabha disapproves it by a simple majority.
accepted.x: The President may revoke a National Emergency at any time. If the Lok Sabha disapproves it by a simple majority, the President must revoke it.
accepted.tq: Identify who may revoke and distinguish discretionary revocation from mandatory revocation.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: If at least one-tenth of the total members of the Lok Sabha give notice of disapproval of a National Emergency, a special sitting of the Lok Sabha must be held within:
accepted.x: A notice by at least one-tenth of the Lok Sabha members requires a special sitting within 14 days to consider disapproval of the Emergency.
accepted.tq: Test the linked pair of threshold and time limit: one-tenth and fourteen days.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding judicial review of a proclamation under Article 352:
1. The 38th Constitutional Amendment made the President’s satisfaction non-justiciable.
2. The bar on judicial review was subsequently reversed.
3. In Minerva Mills, the Supreme Court held that the proclamation could be reviewed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The 38th Amendment attempted to make the satisfaction non-justiciable; this position was later reversed, and Minerva Mills affirmed that the proclamation is reviewable.
accepted.tq: Arrange the legal development as an amendment, reversal and judicial ruling.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (National Emergency)
A. First proclamation
B. Second proclamation
C. Third proclamation

List-II (Year or date)
I. 25 June 1975
II. 1962
III. 1971

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: The first National Emergency was proclaimed in 1962, the second in 1971, and the third on 25 June 1975.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure chronological pair and then eliminate the remaining codes.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Emergency proclaimed in 1962 was associated with:
o: Internal disturbance arising from an election dispute
accepted.x: The first National Emergency, proclaimed in 1962, was based on Chinese aggression and the resulting war.
accepted.tq: Match each emergency instance with its specific ground rather than merely its year.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Emergency of 1971 was proclaimed on the ground of:
o: Failure of a State to comply with Union directions
External aggression connected with the Indo-Pak war
accepted.x: The 1971 Emergency was proclaimed on the ground of external aggression in the context of the Indo-Pak war.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the grounds and circumstances of the 1962, 1971 and 1975 proclamations.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The National Emergency proclaimed on 25 June 1975 was based on the then constitutional ground of:
accepted.x: The 1975 proclamation invoked “internal disturbance,” the expression that was later replaced by “armed rebellion” through the 44th Amendment.
accepted.tq: Use the date to identify the constitutional terminology applicable at that time.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which event immediately preceded the proclamation of the National Emergency in June 1975 and formed an important background to it?
o: The Allahabad High Court voided Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election.
The Lok Sabha passed a resolution of no confidence against the Union Cabinet.
The Supreme Court struck down the 42nd Amendment.
The Election Commission postponed the general election indefinitely.
accepted.x: The Allahabad High Court judgment voiding Indira Gandhi’s 1971 election formed the immediate political background to the 1975 Emergency.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional event to its immediate triggering political development.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 39th Constitutional Amendment Act, enacted during the Emergency period, placed which disputes beyond the jurisdiction of courts?
o: Disputes relating to elections of the President and Vice-President only
All disputes concerning State Legislative Assemblies
Election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker
Disputes relating to the proclamation of Financial Emergency
accepted.x: The 39th Amendment placed election disputes concerning the Prime Minister and the Speaker beyond the courts.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with the particular constitutional office affected, not a neighbouring office.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was a consequence of the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
o: The term of the Lok Sabha was reduced to four years.
The terms of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies were raised to six years.
The President’s power to proclaim Emergency was abolished.
The Rajya Sabha was made subject to dissolution every five years.
accepted.x: The 42nd Amendment, popularly called the “mini-Constitution,” raised the terms of the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies to six years.
accepted.tq: Identify the specific institutional change associated with the “mini-Constitution.”
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: From 26 June 2026, 25 June is observed as:
accepted.x: 25 June is observed as “Samvidhan Hatya Diwas” in remembrance of the proclamation of the 1975 Emergency.
accepted.tq: Test the exact official commemorative expression rather than a near-synonym.
accepted.sec: ■ National Emergency - grounds, written cabinet advice, approval, revocation, instances  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The decision in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India was delivered by a Bench comprising:
accepted.x: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India was decided by a nine-judge Constitution Bench.
accepted.tq: Test a precise judicial composition figure using nearby Constitution Bench sizes as distractors.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the principles laid down in S.R. Bommai v. Union of India:
1. A proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review.
2. The Governor’s opinion is the conclusive test of majority in the Assembly.
3. The floor test in the Assembly is the proper test of majority.
4. A court can restore a dismissed State government in an appropriate case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. The Governor’s opinion is not conclusive; majority must ordinarily be tested on the floor of the Assembly.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap by distinguishing the Governor’s assessment from the Assembly floor test.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under the principles laid down in S.R. Bommai, a proclamation under Article 356 may be invalidated by a court when it is based on:
o: A mere change in the ruling party at the Union level
Any political disagreement between the State and Union Governments
The failure of a State Legislature to pass an ordinary Bill
accepted.x: The proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review, particularly where it is mala fide or founded on irrelevant grounds.
accepted.tq: Apply the judicial-review principle to distinguish constitutionally relevant grounds from political disagreement.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles

accepted.s: A Governor reports that a Ministry has lost its majority, but the Chief Minister requests a floor test. According to S.R. Bommai, the decisive test should ordinarily be:
o: An opinion poll conducted by the Election Commission
A report of the Union Cabinet alone
A vote on the floor of the Legislative Assembly
accepted.x: S.R. Bommai established that the floor of the Assembly, rather than the Governor’s personal opinion, is the proper test of majority.
accepted.tq: Use the “who would do this job?” method to identify the constitutionally appropriate forum.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding dissolution of a State Legislative Assembly under Article 356 is NOT correct?
o: A court may restore a dismissed government in an appropriate case.
The Assembly may initially be kept under suspension until parliamentary approval.
The Assembly must invariably be dissolved immediately after the proclamation.
accepted.x: Immediate and automatic dissolution is not required. The Assembly may remain suspended until Parliament approves, and arbitrary dissolution is impermissible.
accepted.tq: Find the absolute statement that contradicts the Bommai safeguards.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched in the context of S.R. Bommai v. Union of India?
o: Secularism — an ordinary statutory principle only
Federalism — not a feature of the Constitution
Secularism and federalism — basic features of the Constitution
Governor’s opinion — conclusive proof of majority
accepted.x: The judgment recognised secularism and federalism as basic features of the Constitution. It also held that a State government acting against secularism may be dismissed, subject to constitutional and judicial safeguards.
accepted.tq: Pair constitutional doctrines with their status and eliminate the reversed descriptions.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles

accepted.s: A State government acting against the principle of secularism may, subject to constitutional requirements, be:
o: Removed only by the Supreme Court through impeachment proceedings
Suspended permanently by the Governor without parliamentary approval
accepted.x: S.R. Bommai recognised secularism as a basic feature and held that a State government acting against it may be dismissed under Article 356, subject to constitutional safeguards.
accepted.tq: Connect a basic feature of the Constitution with the constitutional consequence recognised by the Court.
accepted.sec: ■ S.R. Bommai v Union of India (1994) - bench, principles

accepted.s: Under Article 360, a Financial Emergency may be proclaimed when the financial stability or credit of:
o: India alone is threatened, but not any part of India
Only the banking system of a State is threatened
India or any part of its territory is threatened
Any part of India alone is threatened, but not India as a whole
accepted.x: Article 360 applies where the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
accepted.tq: Test the constitutional wording “India or any part thereof” without narrowing the scope.
accepted.sec: ■ Financial Emergency - Article 360 consequences, instances  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the parliamentary approval requirement for a Financial Emergency?
o: Approval within one month by special majority
Approval within six months by special majority
Approval within two months by simple majority
Approval within three months by absolute majority
accepted.x: A proclamation of Financial Emergency must be approved by Parliament within two months by a simple majority.
accepted.tq: Separate Article 360’s two-month simple-majority rule from Article 352’s one-month special-majority rule.
accepted.sec: ■ Financial Emergency - Article 360 consequences, instances  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about a Financial Emergency:
1. The Constitution prescribes no maximum period for its continuance.
2. It continues until revoked.
3. It has been proclaimed several times in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. A Financial Emergency has never been declared in India, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Use the exception in the final statement to distinguish constitutional possibility from actual practice.
accepted.sec: ■ Financial Emergency - Article 360 consequences, instances  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a consequence that may follow the proclamation of a Financial Emergency?
o: Automatic dissolution of all State Legislative Assemblies
Reservation of State Money Bills and Financial Bills for the President’s consideration
Directions regarding canons of financial propriety
Reduction of salaries of government servants, including judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts
accepted.x: Article 360 does not provide for automatic dissolution of State Legislative Assemblies. It permits directions on financial propriety, salary reductions and reservation of specified State Bills for the President.
accepted.tq: Find the consequence borrowed from Article 356 rather than Article 360.
accepted.sec: ■ Financial Emergency - Article 360 consequences, instances  [other exams]

accepted.s: During a Financial Emergency, directions issued by the Union may require observance of:
accepted.x: Article 360 permits the Union to issue directions to States to observe specified canons of financial propriety.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact constitutional expression instead of a related but different institutional principle.
accepted.sec: ■ Financial Emergency - Article 360 consequences, instances  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the effect of Article 365?
o: Failure by a State to comply with Union directions may enable the President to hold that the State government cannot be carried on according to the Constitution.
Article 365 applies only to directions issued by the Supreme Court.
Article 365 prevents the Union from issuing directions under Articles 256 and 257.
Every disagreement with a Union direction automatically dissolves the State Legislature.
accepted.x: When a State fails to comply with directions issued under a constitutional provision, such as Articles 256 or 257, the President may conclude that the State government cannot be carried on constitutionally, leading to Article 356 action.
accepted.tq: Follow the constitutional chain from non-compliance to the possible use of Article 356.
accepted.sec: ■ Article 365 - failure to comply with Union directions

accepted.s: Articles 256 and 257 are mentioned in relation to Article 365 because they concern:
o: Directions that may be issued by the Union to States
Appointment of Governors by the President
Financial relations between the Union and States only
accepted.x: Articles 256 and 257 contain provisions under which the Union may issue directions to States; failure to comply may attract the consequence contemplated by Article 365.
accepted.tq: Match the cited Articles with their subject rather than with other emergency provisions.
accepted.sec: ■ Article 365 - failure to comply with Union directions

accepted.s: The emergency provisions of the Indian Constitution were substantially inspired by the:
accepted.x: The Government of India Act, 1935 is regarded as the source of the emergency provisions incorporated in the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Use the source-country/source-statute association without confusing it with the constitutional model for Fundamental Rights.
accepted.sec: ■ Emergency provisions → source country and earlier Act

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched with its source?
o: Emergency provisions — Government of India Act, 1935; ordinance power — Government of India Act, 1935
Emergency provisions — Weimar Constitution; ordinance power — Government of India Act, 1919
Suspension of Fundamental Rights — Government of India Act, 1935; emergency provisions — Weimar Constitution
Emergency provisions — Charter Act, 1833; ordinance power — Weimar Constitution
accepted.x: The emergency provisions and the ordinance power under Articles 123 and 213 are both regarded as relics of the Government of India Act, 1935. The Weimar Constitution is associated with suspension of Fundamental Rights during an emergency.
accepted.tq: Separate the common source of two constitutional features from the distinct German source of another feature.
accepted.sec: ■ Emergency provisions → source country and earlier Act

accepted.s: The provision relating to suspension of Fundamental Rights during an emergency was inspired by the Constitution of:
accepted.x: The emergency-related suspension of Fundamental Rights was inspired by the Weimar Constitution of Germany.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the foreign sources of different constitutional provisions.
accepted.sec: ■ Emergency provisions → source country and earlier Act

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about the current relevance of President’s Rule is correct?
o: President’s Rule can never continue during deferred State elections.
President’s Rule in Manipur was extended till February 2026.
The extension in Manipur was made under Article 360.
President’s Rule in Manipur was constitutionally prohibited after 2024.
accepted.x: President’s Rule in Manipur was reported as extended till February 2026. Such action concerns Article 356, not the Financial Emergency provision under Article 360.
accepted.tq: Check the State, time limit and applicable Article together in a current-affairs constitutional question.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: The criticism that deferred State elections could prolong President’s Rule is particularly connected with a possible conflict involving:
accepted.x: The concern about deferred State elections prolonging President’s Rule is linked to the constitutional limitation associated with Article 356(5).
accepted.tq: Identify the relevant Article by connecting the policy scenario with the specific constitutional limitation.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: Which one of the following is widely regarded as one of the most controversial provisions of the Indian Constitution?
accepted.x: Article 356, dealing with failure of constitutional machinery in a State and President’s Rule, is among the most controversial provisions of the Constitution.
accepted.tq: Use the exact constitutional provision associated with the stated controversy.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: The 1973 spell of President’s Rule in Andhra Pradesh ended after the implementation of the:
accepted.x: The 1973 spell of President’s Rule in Andhra Pradesh ended after the Six-Point Formula.
accepted.tq: Match a State-specific constitutional episode with the regional political settlement that ended it.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles

accepted.s: The Six-Point Formula relating to the 1973 Andhra Pradesh episode was validated through the:
accepted.x: The Six-Point Formula was validated by the 32nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1973, which inserted Article 371D. The 33rd Amendment concerned resignation of legislators.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the closely numbered 32nd and 33rd Amendments by their subject matter.
accepted.sec: ■ Universal angles
